endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: a manufacturer 337 must “establish and maintain procedures for validating the device design,” which “shall ensure 338 that devices conform to defined user needs and intended uses and shall include testing of 339 production units under actual or simulated use conditions”

endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Therefore, CDRH stated that it will be important for manufacturers to consider how to effectively evaluate and monitor the GenAI-enabled device, and the underlying foundation model as applicable, for its specific intended use in a way that can ensure that device accuracy, relevance, and reliability are maintained, once deployed.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: For quality control of the AI decisions, uncertainty estimates should be provided (and calibrated53) to inform the end users about the degree of confidence in the results.54

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Engage in internal and external evaluations, GAI red-teaming, impact assessments, or other structured human feedback exercises in consultation with representative AI Actors with expertise and familiarity in the context of use, and/or who are representative of the populations associated with the context of use.

endorsements.title: HealthBench: Advancing AI evaluation in healthcare, but not yet clinically ready
endorsements.quote: To better reflect clinical reality, future benchmark items should align more closely with end-to-end care, considering the full picture of history, physical examination, diagnostic testing, and care coordination.

endorsements.title: Moving beyond the benchmarks: Five foundational principles for meaningful AI evaluation in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Evaluation frameworks must directly assess performance on the specific clinical tasks for which an AI model is intended to be used ( Fig 1 ).

evidence.title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Deployed LLM performance on multi-turn stroke history-taking, urgency, and safety versus exam-style benchmarks
evidence.effect: Eighteen models evaluated; top model scored 87.4% with zero critical mistakes, only two met safety threshold (≥80%, zero critical mistakes); eleven models made 17 critical mistakes despite strong exam-level knowledge.
evidence.quote: Two leaders met the safety threshold.

evidence.title: Evaluating Fine-Tuned and Base Language Models in Maternal and Vaccination Healthcare for African Settings
evidence.outcome: Fine-tuned vs base LLM ratings by physicians on domain-specific health questions, including critical issues
evidence.effect: MamaBot-Llama improved 4.9% overall (p<.001) with critical issues down 50%; Vax-Llama declined 5.2% overall (p<.001), critical issues up 192%, safety concerns up 400%.
evidence.quote: Rigorous domain-specific validation is essential before clinical deployment.

evidence.title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
evidence.outcome: diagnostic-question versus clinical-procedure performance
evidence.effect: Models performed well on diagnostic questions but underperformed in clinical procedures; no numeric effect reported.
evidence.quote: Although these models performed well in answering diagnostic questions, they consistently underperformed in clinical diagnostic procedures and exhibited a significant number of clinical errors.

evidence.title: Clinical reasoning in large language models under ecologically valid conditions
evidence.outcome: LLM clinical reasoning in an interactive simulation versus constrained formats, including information-seeking and deferral
evidence.effect: All six LLMs met preregistered performance thresholds across 15 cases with no failures on critical safety demands; information-seeking and deferral behaviors were consistently expressed.
evidence.quote: Under conditions that permit information-seeking and deferral, such behaviors are consistently expressed.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated clinical cases (six LLMs evaluated on each)

evidence.title: Evaluating Diagnostic Accuracy and Clinical Reasoning of Multiple Large Language Models in Psychiatry
evidence.outcome: association of clinician-rated reasoning quality with diagnostic correctness in LLM psychiatric diagnosis
evidence.effect: Reasoning quality strongly associated with diagnostic correctness (β = 1·80; p < 0·001); data extraction quality alone was not. Best model top-5 accuracy 0·801.
evidence.quote: Clinician-rated diagnostic reasoning quality was strongly associated with diagnostic correctness in mixed-effects logistic regression analyses (β = 1·80; p < 0·001), whereas data extraction quality alone was not.

evidence.title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT in Healthcare: Non-English Clinical Environment for Retinal Vascular Disease Classification
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic F1 on real clinical reports versus ophthalmologists and interns
evidence.effect: Best ChatGPT F1 80.05% (English prompt, direct diagnosis), below ophthalmologists (89.35%) but close to interns (82.69%); performance gaps remain
evidence.quote: ChatGPT using English prompt for direct diagnosis achieved the best performance, with F1-score of 80.05%, which was inferior to ophthalmologists (89.35%) but close to ophthalmologist interns (82.69%).

evidence.title: Large language models to help appeal denied radiotherapy services
evidence.outcome: Benchmarking of LLM configurations on an intended-use task with blinded expert scoring
evidence.effect: GPT-4 and GPT-4web letters demonstrated superior clinical reasoning and were readier for submission than GPT-3.5 letters (p < 0.001); fine-tuned GPT-3.5ft performed worse across all domains (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: GPT-4 and GPT-4web letters demonstrated superior clinical reasoning and were readier for submission than GPT-3.5 letters (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated test prompts (appeal letters per LLM)

evidence.title: Reproducible Generative AI Evaluation for Healthcare: A Clinician-in-the-Loop Approach
evidence.outcome: Benchmarking deployed generative AI on clinical queries with SME ratings
evidence.effect: Of 633 queries, 614 (96.99%) produced evaluable responses; correctness 95.5%, query comprehension 98.6%, helpful 94.4%.
evidence.quote: Results demonstrated high rates of response correctness (95.5%) and query comprehension (98.6%), with 94.4% of responses rated as helpful.

evidence.title: An AI Dietitian for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Based on Large Language and Image Recognition Models: Preclinical Concept Validation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on dietitian exam and expert-reviewed responses to common medical nutrition therapy questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT and GPT 4.0 passed the Chinese Registered Dietitian exam; dietitians rated 162 of 168 ChatGPT responses favorably; recommendations mostly aligned except root vegetables and dry beans.
evidence.quote: Professional dietitians' reviews of ChatGPT's responses to common questions were largely positive, with 162 out of 168 providing favorable reviews.
evidence.sample_unit: patients surveyed (plus 168 dietitian reviews of ChatGPT responses and exam questions)

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models as clinical laboratory test recommenders in primary and emergency care: a crucial step in clinical decision making
evidence.outcome: Precision and recall of GPT-4o lab test orders versus expert consensus gold standard on simulated cases
evidence.effect: Precision was moderate to high (68-82 %) but recall was lower (41-51 %), indicating a risk of underutilization; prompting strategy, complexity, and setting did not significantly affect performance.
evidence.quote: Precision was moderate to high for both prompting strategies (68-82 %), although relatively lower recall (41-51 %) highlighted a risk of underutilization.

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek for non-critical triage support using real-world conversations in emergency department
evidence.outcome: LLM triage accuracy against nurse-assigned KTAS on real-world conversations across models
evidence.effect: Among 1,057 real triage cases, Gemini 2.5 flash reached 73.8% accuracy and Gemini 2.5 pro 90.9% sensitivity; performance varied widely across models and versions.
evidence.quote: Performance varied widely between models and even between different versions from the same vendor.

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of a Medical Large Language Model in Answering Real-World Radiation Oncology Questions: Multicenter Observational Study
evidence.outcome: LLM answer quality vs experts on real-world clinical questions, rather than exam-style
evidence.effect: No significant quality difference between LLM and clinical experts (mean 3.38 vs 3.63; P=.26); harmful in 13% expert vs 16% LLM answers (P=.63).
evidence.quote: There were no significant differences between the quality of the answers between LLM and clinical experts (mean scores of 3.38 vs 3.63; median 4.00, IQR 3.00-4.00 vs median 3.67, IQR 3.33-4.00; P=.26; Wilcoxon signed rank test).

evidence.title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: raw-report treatment decision performance
evidence.effect: Original medical reports: Cohen κ -0.47 to 0.22; ICC 0.0-1.0; FBI 0.95-1.51.
evidence.quote: When presented with original medical reports, LLMs showed poor performance (Cohen κ coefficient: -0.47 to 0.22; ICC: 0.0-1.0; FBI: 0.95-1.51).

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Point-in-Time Interpretation of Advanced Hemodynamics in Liver Transplant Recipients: A Pilot Evaluation of Content Quality and Safety
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated content quality and catastrophic risk of ChatGPT interpretations of intraoperative hemodynamic screenshots
evidence.effect: Median domain scores 4.6 to 4.8; more than 90% of ratings satisfactory; 86% of catastrophic Risk ratings scored 0, with only three isolated high-risk assessments.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated consistently high performance across all content-quality domains, with median scores ranging from 4.6 to 4.8 and more than 90% of all ratings classified as satisfactory.
evidence.sample_unit: hemodynamic monitor screenshots (frames) from 5 liver transplant recipients, each rated by 5 anesthesiologists

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models in supporting autoimmune liver disease diagnosis and clinical decision-making: advantages of reasoning-based models
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy, safety, and diagnostic performance on AILD questions and real-world cases, by model
evidence.effect: o1-preview had the greatest proportion of accurate responses (78.3%), highest mean safety score; diagnostic accuracy 81.0%, outperforming GPT-4o and GPT-3.5-Turbo.
evidence.quote: In diagnostic testing, the o1-preview achieved an overall accuracy of 81.0%, outperforming GPT-4o and GPT-3.5-Turbo, particularly in single-entity AILD diagnoses.

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of large language model recommendations in melanoma: comparison with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions in a real-world cohort
evidence.outcome: LLM melanoma treatment recommendations rated against real MDT decisions across five domains
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-5 Thinking performed best, followed by ChatGPT-4o; Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 rated less favorably; differences significant across all domains, largest in adjuvant/systemic treatment scenarios.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-5 Thinking showed the strongest and most consistent overall performance, followed by ChatGPT-4o, while Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 were rated less favorably.

evidence.title: OpenAIs HealthBench in Action: Evaluating an LLM-Based Medical Assistant on Realistic Clinical Queries
evidence.outcome: Deployed agentic RAG assistant scored on rubric-based HealthBench Hard clinical competencies vs frontier LLMs
evidence.effect: DR. INFO scored 0.68 on HealthBench Hard vs GPT-5 0.46, GPT-5.2 0.42, GPT-5.1 0.40, Grok 3 0.23, Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.19, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.02; 0.72 in a 100-sample comparison against OpenEvidence and Pathway.md.
evidence.quote: On the Hard subset of 1,000 challenging examples, DR. INFO achieves a HealthBench Hard score of 0.68, outperforming leading frontier LLMs including the GPT-5 model family (GPT-5: 0.46, GPT-5.2: 0.42, GPT-5.1: 0.40), Grok 3 (0.23), Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.19), and Claude 3.7 Sonnet (0.02) across all behavioral axes (accuracy, completeness, instruction following, etc.).

evidence.title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
evidence.outcome: Rubric-based completeness of LLMs on real patient pancreatic cancer questions versus exam-style performance
evidence.effect: Rubric completeness ranged from 46.5% to 82.3% across 22 LLMs despite expert-level exam performance; newer reasoning models did not consistently improve factuality.
evidence.quote: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved expert-level performance on standardized examinations, yet multiple-choice accuracy poorly reflects real-world clinical utility and safety.
evidence.sample_unit: authentic patient questions (3,130 expert rubric criteria)

evidence.title: Evaluation format, not model capability, drives triage failure in the assessment of consumer health AI
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy under exam-style versus naturalistic patient-style evaluation of the same LLMs
evidence.effect: Naturalistic interaction improved triage accuracy by 6.4 percentage points (p = 0.015); asthma triage improved from 48% to 80%; three models scored 0-24% with forced choice but 100% with free text.
evidence.quote: Naturalistic interaction improved triage accuracy by 6.4 percentage points ($p = 0.015$).

evidence.title: Beyond Accuracy: An Efficiency- and Safety-Aware Framework for Evaluating Clinical AI with Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Whether traditional metrics and benchmarks reflect clinical utility of LLM responses to pharmacology scenarios
evidence.effect: BLEU 0.003–0.024 and ROUGE-L 0.079–0.166 failed to reflect clinical utility; CVD framework exposed efficiency–safety trade-offs; GPT-4o safety 0.437 (moderate).
evidence.quote: Traditional metrics (BLEU: 0.003–0.024; ROUGE-L: 0.079–0.166) failed to reflect clinical utility, while the CVD framework exposed critical efficiency–safety trade-offs.

evidence.title: A Three-Tier Operational Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Hospital Medication Safety
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on hospital medication-safety scenarios (F1, sensitivity, specificity) across 40 models
evidence.effect: F1 78.5%–92.3%, accuracy 65.4%–89.8%, sensitivity 81.4%–100.0%, specificity 6.1%–81.8%; three models had 100% sensitivity but below 25% specificity, like an always-alert classifier.
evidence.quote: Headline binary performance on the full benchmark spans a wide range across the 40 models: F1 78.5%–92.3%, accuracy 65.4%–89.8%, sensitivity 81.4%–100.0%, specificity 6.1%–81.8%.

evidence.title: Quality of Answers of Generative Large Language Models Versus Peer Users for Interpreting Laboratory Test Results for Lay Patients: Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM answer quality (relevance, correctness, helpfulness, safety) on patient lab-result questions versus peers and other LLMs
evidence.effect: GPT-4 scored better than all other LLMs and human answers on all 4 aspects, but some GPT-4 responses were inaccurate or not individualized.
evidence.quote: The results of the win rate and medical expert evaluation both showed that GPT-4's responses achieved better scores than all the other LLM responses and human responses on all 4 aspects (relevance, correctness, helpfulness, and safety).

evidence.title: Domain-Specific Customization for Language Models in Otolaryngology: The ENT GPT Assistant
evidence.outcome: MCQ accuracy of customized otolaryngology LLM versus general LLMs and otolaryngologists
evidence.effect: E-GPT-A overall accuracy 74.6% vs GPT-3.5 60.4%, Claude 2.0 61.7%, Claude 2.1 60.8%, GPT-4 68.3%; otolaryngologists and trainees averaged 71.1%. Lower in pediatrics (62.5%) and facial plastics (67.5%).
evidence.quote: E-GPT-A achieved an overall accuracy of 74.6%, outperforming GPT-3.5 (60.4%), Claude 2.0 (61.7%), Claude 2.1 (60.8%), and GPT-4 (68.3%).

evidence.title: Evaluating and enhancing the performance of large language models in thyroid eye disease through customization and Chain-of-Thought strategies
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of customized deployed LLM configurations on TED multiple-choice questions versus base models
evidence.effect: GPT-4 76.2% and Claude 3.5 83.2%; customized TED-GPT 86.1% and TED-Claude 89.1%, outperforming newer LLMs.
evidence.quote: The addition of CoT, along with customization into GPT-4 and Claude 3.5, led to improvement in the accuracy (CoT-GPT 86.1%, CoT-Claude 87.1%, TED-GPT 86.1%, TED-Claude 89.1%), outperforming all other newer LLMs.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Crisis Detection: A Real-World Benchmark from Psychological Support Hotlines
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on real-world crisis transcripts across four tasks
evidence.effect: F1 0.880 suicidal ideation, 0.779 suicide plan, 0.907 risk assessment; mood recognition max F1 0.709.
evidence.quote: LLMs showed strong results in suicidal ideation detection (F1 = 0.880), suicide plan identification (F1 = 0.779), and risk assessment (F1 = 0.907), with notable gains from few shot prompting and fine-tuning.

evidence.title: Multimodal LLM-driven IoT digital healthcare platform for intelligent dysphagia dietary monitoring
evidence.outcome: Safety-relevant IDDSI texture classification of deployed MLLM pipeline on clinician-verified meal image benchmark
evidence.effect: Qwen-based pipeline exact match accuracy 61.74%, lowest total false negative rate of 9.2% among 14 models; local open-source models had 100% FNR for liquids versus 7.14% for the cloud system.
evidence.quote: Our Qwen-based pipeline achieved a total exact match accuracy of 61.74%.

evidence.title: DiagnosticXchange: an open-source framework for evaluating safety, efficiency, and diagnostic reasoning in clinical AI systems
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Whether accuracy-only benchmarks reveal differences among deployed AI systems in cost, safety, effort
evidence.effect: Three systems had near-identical accuracy (93.5%-94.0%) but differed significantly in cost (1.75-fold) and 2.1-fold in physician oversight; multi-dimensional evaluation revealed differences invisible to existing benchmarks.
evidence.quote: DiagnosticXchange provides an open-source, reproducible framework for multi-dimensional assessment that reveals clinically consequential differences invisible to existing benchmarks.

evidence.title: CNS-Obsidian: A Neurosurgical Vision-Language Model Built From Scientific Publications
evidence.outcome: Domain VLM accuracy on synthetic versus human-generated questions compared with GPT-4o
evidence.effect: Matched GPT-4o on synthetic questions (76.13% vs 77.54%, P = .235) but only 46.81% on human-generated questions vs GPT-4o's 65.70% (P < 10-15)
evidence.quote: CNS-Obsidian matched GPT-4o on synthetic questions (76.13% vs 77.54%, P = .235), but only achieved 46.81% accuracy on human-generated questions vs GPT-4o's 65.70% (P < 10-15).

evidence.title: Adoption and Use of LLMs at an Academic Medical Center
evidence.outcome: Adequacy of benchmark-based evaluation for monitoring the deployed LLM interface
evidence.effect: Benchmark-based evaluations were insufficient for monitoring and evaluating the UI, so new monitoring methods were required.
evidence.quote: Benchmark-based evaluations proved insufficient for monitoring and evaluation of the UI, requiring new methods to monitor performance.

evidence.title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
evidence.outcome: Whether medical knowledge benchmark performance predicts clinical safety of deployed AI tools
evidence.effect: Despite strong performance on medical knowledge benchmarks, widely used AI tools can produce consultation advice with potential for severe harm.
evidence.quote: Collectively, these results show that despite strong performance on medical knowledge benchmarks, widely used AI tools can produce medical consultation advice with the potential for severe harm, and highlight the need for explicit measurement of clinical safety.

evidence.title: Prompt engineering does not universally improve Large Language Model performance across clinical decision-making tasks
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on real-world clinical decision tasks versus knowledge assessments
evidence.effect: Near-perfect accuracy in final diagnosis, poor performance in relevant diagnostic testing, and moderate performance in remaining tasks across three LLMs.
evidence.quote: All models showed high variability by task, achieving near-perfect accuracy in final diagnosis, poor performance in relevant diagnostic testing, and moderate performance in remaining tasks.

evidence.title: SycoEval-EM: Sycophancy Evaluation of Large Language Models in Simulated Clinical Encounters for Emergency Care
evidence.outcome: Whether static medical benchmark performance, scale, or recency predicted robustness to patient pressure
evidence.effect: Model scale, recency, and static benchmark performance did not consistently predict robustness; static benchmarks judged insufficient to predict safety under sustained social pressure.
evidence.quote: Model scale, recency, and performance on static medical benchmarks did not consistently predict robustness.

evidence.title: Are Multimodal LLMs Ready for Clinical Dermatology? A Real-World Evaluation in Dermatology
evidence.outcome: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy on public benchmarks versus real-world consultation cases
evidence.effect: Public benchmarks: top-3 accuracy 26.55% best open-weight, 42.25% GPT-4.1. Real-world images alone: 1.50%-13.35% open-weight, 24.65% GPT-4.1.
evidence.quote: These findings demonstrate that benchmark performance substantially overestimates the real-world clinical capability of current dermatology MLLMs.

evidence.title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on diagnostic questions versus full clinical diagnostic procedures
evidence.effect: Models performed well answering diagnostic questions but consistently underperformed in clinical diagnostic procedures and exhibited a significant number of clinical errors.
evidence.quote: Although these models performed well in answering diagnostic questions, they consistently underperformed in clinical diagnostic procedures and exhibited a significant number of clinical errors.

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of State‑of‑the‑Art Large Language Models for Patient Education Prior to Interventional Radiology procedures
evidence.outcome: Radiologist-rated accuracy (5-point Likert) of LLM answers to IR procedure patient questions
evidence.effect: OpenBioLLM-8b (BEST 3.51, CT-HDR 3.32, TAPE 3.34) and BioMistral-7b (BEST 2.92, CT-HDR 3.03, TAPE 3.33) scored significantly worse than DeepSeek-V3 and ChatGPT-4o (DeepSeek BEST 4.49, CT-HDR 4.24).
evidence.quote: In contrast, OpenBioLLM-8b (BEST 3.51 (± 1.15), CT-HDR 3.32 (± 1.13), TAPE 3.34 (± 1.16)) and BioMistral-7b (BEST 2.92 (± 1.35), CT-HDR 3.03 (± 1.06), TAPE 3.33 (± 1.28)) performed significantly worse than DeepSeek-V3 and ChatGPT-4o across all procedures.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence Application in the Diagnosis of Pneumothorax on Chest Radiograph Interpretation
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o pneumothorax detection accuracy and sensitivity on chest radiographs versus expert consensus
evidence.effect: Accuracy 83.7%, sensitivity 70.9%, specificity 96.4%, NPV 76.8%; AUC 0.894 for large vs 0.439 for small pneumothoraces.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic performance was higher for large pneumothoraces (AUC: 0.894) compared to small pneumothoraces (AUC: 0.439).

evidence.title: ChatGPT vs DeepSeek: A Comparative Study of Diagnostic Accuracy and Clinical Reasoning in Rare and Complex Diseases
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs on rare and complex disease case reports
evidence.effect: Diagnostic accuracy ranged between 30.0% and 40.0%, no significant differences among models (P = 0.16); ChatGPT-o1 12/30 (40.0%), DeepSeek-R1 9/30 (30.0%).
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy, the primary outcome, ranged between 30.0% and 40.0% with no significant differences observed among models (Cochran’s Q test, P = 0.16).

evidence.title: Clinical Usability of Generative Artificial Intelligence for MR Safety Advice
evidence.outcome: Clinical usability of generative AI answers to MR safety requests versus human expert, by expert panel
evidence.effect: 93% (28/30) human, 50% (15/30) GAIO and 43% (13/30) ChatGPT responses deemed acceptable for clinical use; AIs significantly lower than human MRSE.
evidence.quote: Overall, 93% (28/30) of the human responses, 50% (15/30) of the GAIO responses and 43% (13/30) of the ChatGPT responses were deemed acceptable for clinical use.

evidence.title: Performance Evaluation of Large Language Models in Real-World Perinatal Medication Consultations: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on real-world perinatal medication consultation questions, rated by pharmacologists
evidence.effect: Significant overall differences among models (p<0.001); GPT-5.1 highest total score (9.1 ± 0.8), accuracy 9.2 ± 0.7; gaps larger in complex scenarios with comorbidities or benefit–risk trade-offs.
evidence.quote: Performance gaps were more pronounced in complex clinical scenarios involving comorbidities or benefit–risk trade-offs, whereas domestic models demonstrated relative advantages in consultations involving traditional Chinese medicine.

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Automated Icd-10 Coding of Obstetric Clinical Notes in Portuguese: Comparison With Human Coders
evidence.outcome: LLM ICD-10 coding agreement with human reference on real-world clinical notes
evidence.effect: Best model GPT-4o reached micro-F1 0.36 at three-character level and 0.15 at leaf level against the human reference.
evidence.quote: Even the best-performing model (GPT-4o) achieved only modest agreement with the human reference, with micro-F1 scores of 0.36 at the three-character level and 0.15 at the leaf level.

evidence.title: Benchmarking General-Purpose and Medical AI Large Language Models for Clinical Assessment and Management in Parkinson’s Disease
evidence.outcome: Clinical appropriateness of LLM assessments and management plans for Parkinson's vignettes
evidence.effect: Appropriate assessments 80.0% (Gemini) vs 86.7% (OpenEvidence); management plans 48.9% vs 57.8%; severe errors in plans 26.7% in both.
evidence.quote: Gemini 1.5 Pro and OpenEvidence showed high rates of clinically appropriate assessments (80.0% vs. 86.7%) but lower performance in management plans (48.9% vs. 57.8%).

evidence.title: Boundary-Specific Failure Modes and Safety Trade-offs of Large Language Models in Chronic Kidney Disease Renoprotective Therapy Review: A Stratified Synthetic Benchmark
evidence.outcome: Aggregate sensitivity concealing boundary-specific performance differences in RASi omission detection
evidence.effect: RASi detection at eGFR<15: Grok 85%, GPT-5.4 55%, Gemini 10%, DeepSeek 10%, despite near-ceiling SGLT2i/finerenone sensitivity (97-100%).
evidence.quote: For RASi, performance diverged at the eGFR<15 boundary: Grok 4.1 Fast 85% versus GPT-5.4 55%, Gemini 10%, DeepSeek 10%.

evidence.title: Comparison of the Diagnostic Reliability of ChatGPT in Letournel–Judet Acetabulum Fracture Classification Based on Judet Radiographs According to Orthopaedic Residents
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-4o accuracy on Letournel-Judet acetabular fracture classification versus residents
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 17.9% for ChatGPT-4o vs 88.6% and 91.8% for the two residents; kappa with reference standard -0.014 for ChatGPT-4o.
evidence.quote: The overall diagnostic accuracy for the final Letournel-Judet classification was 17.9% for ChatGPT-4o, compared to 88.6% and 91.8% for the first and second orthopaedic residents, respectively.

evidence.title: Dissecting clinical reasoning failures in frontier artificial intelligence using 10,000 synthetic cases
evidence.outcome: Whether diagnostic competence reflects treatment safety in deployed LLM clinical reasoning
evidence.effect: All LLMs included MS in the differential in >91% of cases, but treatment safety errors were frequent, so diagnostic accuracy did not associate with treatment safety.
evidence.quote: However, diagnostic competence did not associate with treatment safety.

evidence.title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: A Diagnostic Sensor for AI Reasoning Pathology in Sequential Clinical Decision-Making
evidence.outcome: Gap between vignette-benchmark performance and sequential clinical reasoning behavior
evidence.effect: LLMs perform well on complete-vignette benchmarks, but under sequential information delivery they abandon correct diagnoses; 90% access vs 60% retention, invisible under single-shot evaluation.
evidence.quote: Large Language Models achieve impressive accuracy on medical benchmarks that present clinical information as complete vignettes, but their behavior under sequential information delivery, the standard mode of real clinical practice, is poorly characterized.

evidence.title: A Systematic Performance Evaluation of Three Large Language Models in Answering Questions on moderate Hyperthermia
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on specialized clinical domain questions despite general expert-level benchmark claims
evidence.effect: Despite expert-level performance in many medical domains, the three LLMs achieved only 'acceptable' mean quality (3.07-3.26) in moderate hyperthermia, with 15-19% potentially harmful answers.
evidence.quote: Our findings indicate that the performance of LLMs in HT in versions available at the time of investigation is only partially satisfactory.
evidence.sample_unit: expert quality evaluations of LLM responses

evidence.title: Evaluation of four large language models on complex, infectious disease case scenarios
evidence.outcome: Unsafe responses and critical omissions of LLMs on complex ID vignettes rated by ID clinicians
evidence.effect: Unsafe responses: GPT-o1 30%, GPT-4o 40%, Claude 37%; critical omissions: GPT-o1 27%, GPT-4o 43%, Claude 47%. Llama 3.1 8B performed significantly worse on most criteria.
evidence.quote: The open-source, smaller Llama 3.1 8B model performed poorly and large, non-reasoning models varied, but more than 30% of responses containing a risk of harm or critical omission.

evidence.title: Performance, safety, and repeated-query stability of large language models versus early-career urologists in urological oncology: a source-masked vignette benchmark
evidence.outcome: Safety-critical errors in LLM responses to oncology vignettes
evidence.effect: Safety-critical errors occurred in 25.0%, 25.0%, and 26.0% of LLM responses versus 2.0% and 1.0% of urologist responses (Q = 51.34; P < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Safety-critical errors occurred in 25.0%, 25.0%, and 26.0% of LLM responses versus 2.0% and 1.0% of urologist responses (Cochran’s Q = 51.34; P < 0.001); all six human–LLM contrasts remained significant.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Masks Outdated Reasoning: Evaluating LLMs on Evolving Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Whether correct final-answer accuracy reflects valid clinical reasoning
evidence.effect: Rationale valid in only 53.7% of responses despite 89–100% conclusion accuracy in three models.
evidence.quote: Finally, correct final answers substantially overstated the clinical validity of the models’ stated rationale

evidence.title: Errors, Hallucinations, and Clinical Impact of General-Purpose Multimodal Large Language Models in Histopathology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy, errors and hallucinations of general-purpose multimodal LLMs on histopathology cases
evidence.effect: Strict diagnostic accuracy 48.9% overall (36.6% to 58.2% across LLMs); errors in 82.0% of outputs, hallucinations in 76.6%; 90.2% had at least one error or hallucination.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy alone substantially underestimates the safety limitations of general-purpose LLMs in histopathology.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM outputs (153 pathology cases x 4 LLMs)

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT as an Adjunct for the Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making in Primary Breast Cancer Cases
evidence.outcome: Real-case clinical competence of general ChatGPT in tumor board recommendations
evidence.effect: Despite ability to pass medical exams, ChatGPT could not provide specific therapy recommendations for primary breast cancer cases.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT has the potential to find its spot in clinical medicine, but the current version is not able to provide specific recommendations for the therapy of patients with primary breast cancer.
evidence.sample_unit: patient cases (consecutive early breast cancer cases discussed at tumor board)

evidence.title: Applications of GPT-4 for Accurate Diagnosis of Retinal Diseases Through Optical coherence tomography Image Recognition
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy on retinal OCT images versus retinal specialists
evidence.effect: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy was consistently around 26% across four experiments, versus 93.75% for retinal disease specialists.
evidence.quote: In four distinct experiments, the diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4 was consistently around 26%, which showed a significant disparity compared to the diagnostic accuracy of retinal disease specialists (93.75%).

evidence.title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-concordant Treatment Decision-making on Real-world Data
evidence.outcome: performance on typical clinical data
evidence.effect: Original medical reports: kappa −0.47–0.22, ICC 0.0–1.0, FBI 0.95–1.51.
evidence.quote: When presented with original medical reports, LLMs showed poor performance (kappa: −0.47–0.22, ICC: 0.0–1.0, FBI: 0.95–1.51).

evidence.title: A Comparative Study of Predictive model (ECG Buddy) and ChatGPT-4o for Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis via ECG image Analysis: Performance, Accuracy, and Clinical Feasibility
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-4o performance on ECG image MI diagnosis with a general model, and plausibility of explanations
evidence.effect: ChatGPT accuracy 65.95%, sensitivity 36.40%, AUC 57.34%; explanations clinically plausible in 7.5% of 40 cases, 40% completely incorrect.
evidence.quote: In an error analysis of 40 cases, ChatGPT provided clinically plausible explanations in only 7.5% of cases, whereas 35% were partially correct, 40% were completely incorrect, and 17.5% received no meaningful explanation.

evidence.title: Assessing the Utility of ChatGPT Throughout the Entire Clinical Workflow: Development and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT accuracy on clinical vignette tasks across differential diagnosis, testing, final diagnosis, management
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 71.7% (95% CI 69.3%-74.1%); final diagnosis 76.9%; initial differential diagnosis 60.3% (95% CI 54.2%-66.6%).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT achieved an overall accuracy of 71.7% (95% CI 69.3%-74.1%) across all 36 clinical vignettes.

evidence.title: What can GPT-4 do for Diagnosing Rare Eye Diseases? A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy on rare eye disease cases by simulated user scenario
evidence.effect: Simulated patient scenario had no 'right' responses; family physician 50% right; junior ophthalmologist 90% right. Overall 83.3% of 30 responses judged appropriate.
evidence.quote: However, compared to the ground truth, GPT-4 could only output several possible diseases generally without "right" responses in the simulated patient scenarios.
evidence.sample_unit: GPT-4 responses (10 rare eye disease cases x 3 simulated user scenarios)

evidence.title: ChatGPT fails challenging the recent ESCMID brain abscess guideline
evidence.outcome: Whether LLM performance on guideline questions reflects safe clinical competence
evidence.effect: ChatGPT gave recommendations for 17 of 20 challenges, but single responses could possibly harm patients; expert committee remains necessary.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, single responses could possibly harm the patients.
evidence.sample_unit: guideline PECO questions (20 challenges: with and without data prompting)

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: Analyzing the Performance of ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing in Scoliosis Detection and Cobb Angle Assessment
evidence.outcome: General-purpose LLM accuracy on intended-use imaging tasks (scoliosis detection, Cobb angle) versus expert assessment
evidence.effect: ChatGPT detected scoliosis in 100% of images but Bing detected none; ChatGPT accurate for Cobb angle in only 43.5%, with limited accuracy for curve direction, type, and vertebral rotation.
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT had limited effectiveness (43.5%) in assessing Cobb angles, showing significant inaccuracy and discrepancy compared to human assessments.
evidence.sample_unit: posturographic X-ray images of severe single-curve scoliosis

evidence.title: Evaluating GPT-V4 (GPT-4 with Vision) on Detection of Radiologic Findings on Chest Radiographs
evidence.outcome: GPT-4V detection of ICD-10 findings on real-world chest radiographs versus radiologist reference standard
evidence.effect: Zero-shot ICD-10 detection: NIH PPV 12.3%, TPR 5.8%, F1 7.3%; MIDRC PPV 25.0%, TPR 16.8%, F1 18.2%. With laterality, F1 was 4.5% (NIH) and 6.4% (MIDRC).
evidence.quote: Although GPT-4V has shown promise in understanding natural images, it had limited effectiveness in interpreting real-world chest radiographs.

evidence.title: ChatGPT yields low accuracy in determining LI-RADS scores based on free-text and structured radiology reports in German language
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LI-RADS classification by GPT-3.5 against radiologist consensus ground truth
evidence.effect: Accuracy was 53% on unstructured and 44% on structured reports; kappa 0.51 and 0.44.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT at determining LI-RADS categories was poor (53% and 44% on unstructured and structured reports).

evidence.title: A pilot feasibility study comparing large language models in extracting key information from ICU patient text records from an Irish population
evidence.outcome: Performance of LLM summaries on intended-use ICU discharge summary task with local data
evidence.effect: All models had narrative coherence problems and omitted key clinical data; only moderately captured clinically meaningful data in correct order.
evidence.quote: All encountered issues with narrative coherence and omitted key clinical data and only moderately captured all clinically meaningful data in the correct order.
evidence.sample_unit: ICU episodes (one summary per LLM per episode)

evidence.title: The evaluation of the performance of ChatGPT in the management of labor analgesia
evidence.outcome: Clinical decision-making performance of ChatGPT4 versus expert standards despite prior success on knowledge exam questions
evidence.effect: Roughly a quarter of responses to clinical scenarios were unsafe, although the model has answered knowledge-based anesthesia questions with reasonable accuracy.
evidence.quote: In summary, approximately one quarter of all responses by ChatGPT4 were deemed unsafe by expert obstetric anesthesiologists.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (each rated by 7 expert obstetric anesthesiologists)

evidence.title: Assessing GPT-4 multimodal performance in radiological image analysis
evidence.outcome: GPT-4V accuracy identifying modality, anatomical region, and pathology on ER images versus senior radiologists
evidence.effect: Modality 100% (221/221), anatomical region 87.1% (189/217), pathology 35.2% (76/216); pathology accuracy 9.1% in US, 36.4% in CT, 66.7% in X-ray.
evidence.quote: GPT-4V identified the imaging modality correctly in 100% of cases (221/221), the anatomical region in 87.1% (189/217), and the pathology in 35.2% (76/216).
evidence.sample_unit: emergency room diagnostic images (US, CT, X-ray)

evidence.title: APPLICATIONS OF MULTIMODAL GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN A REAL-WORLD RETINA CLINIC SETTING
evidence.outcome: GPT-4V diagnostic accuracy on real-world retina clinic images, open-ended vs multiple-choice
evidence.effect: 13.7% accuracy for open-ended questions and 31.3% for multiple-choice questions; ICD-10 code accuracy 5.5% and 31.3%.
evidence.quote: In 256 eyes from 143 patients, Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4-V demonstrated a 13.7% accuracy for open-ended questions and 31.3% for multiple-choice questions, with International Classification of Diseases 10th revision code accuracies at 5.5% and 31.3%, respectively.

evidence.title: Using Natural Language Processing (GPT-4) for Computed Tomography Image Analysis of Cerebral Hemorrhages in Radiology: Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 identification completeness and misidentification of cerebral hemorrhage types on CT
evidence.effect: Overall identification completeness 72.6% (SD 18.6%); chronic subdural completeness only 37.3%; misidentification 26.2% to 54.0% across hemorrhage types.
evidence.quote: The overall identification completeness percentage for the 6 types of cerebral hemorrhages was 72.6% (SD 18.6%).

evidence.title: Accuracy of a Commercial Large Language Model (ChatGPT) to Perform Disaster Triage of Simulated Patients Using the Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment (START) Protocol: Gage Repeatability and Reproducibility Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of commercial LLM for START disaster triage against specialist reference standard
evidence.effect: Accuracy was 63.9% with 32.9% overtriage and 3.1% undertriage; conclusion that ChatGPT-4 is insufficient for START triage.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT for START was 63.9% with a 32.9% overtriage rate and a 3.1% undertriage rate.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated triages (391 vignettes x 9 prompts x 10 repetitions)

evidence.title: Is Artificial Intelligence a Useful Tool for Clinical Practice of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and quality of ChatGPT Plus answers to oral surgery clinical questions by difficulty level
evidence.effect: Median accuracy 5, 75% scored 4 or above; median quality 4. Hard questions scored lower than easy and medium (accuracy P<0.001, quality P=0.001).
evidence.quote: The median scores of hard-level questions were found to be lower than the easy-level and medium-level questions.

evidence.title: GPT-4-based AI agents-the new expert system for detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms?
evidence.outcome: Non-customized GPT-4 ability to interpret resistance categories and agreement with routine diagnostics
evidence.effect: Non-customized GPT-4 could interpret 169/862 (19.6%) categories; 137/169 (81.1%) agreed with routine diagnostics.
evidence.quote: Non-customized GPT-4 could interpret 169/862 (19.6%) categories, and 137/169 (81.1%) agreed with routine diagnostics.

evidence.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Model Utility in Neuroimaging Clinical Decision Support
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Share of LLM imaging recommendations rated optimal per ACR criteria across eight models
evidence.effect: Optimal recommendations varied widely: GPT4 23/24, ChatGPT 20/24, Perplexity 19/24, Claude 19/24, Bard 1 13/24, Bard 2 14/24, Bing Chat 14/24, Llama 5/24.
evidence.quote: The models varied in their ability to deliver an "optimal" recommendation based on these scenarios as follows: ChatGPT (20/24), GPT4 (23/24), Bard 1 (13/24), Bard 2 (14/24), Bing Chat (14/24), Llama (5/24), Perplexity (19/24), and Claude (19/24).

evidence.title: How soon will surgeons become mere technicians? Chatbot performance in managing clinical scenarios
evidence.venue: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
evidence.outcome: Chatbot critical failures on board-style clinical scenarios versus surgeons
evidence.effect: Critical failures were more frequent for chatbots (median 0.50 per chatbot/scenario vs 0.19 per surgeon/scenario; P = .016).
evidence.quote: Chatbot answers were significantly more likely to be deemed critical failures compared to those provided by surgeons (median, 0.50 per chatbot/scenario vs 0.19 per surgeon/scenario; P = .016).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenarios (each answered by 4 chatbots and 21 board-certified thoracic surgeons)

evidence.title: A pilot evaluation of the diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-3.5 for multiple sclerosis from case reports
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-3.5 for multiple sclerosis from case reports
evidence.effect: Correctly diagnosed MS in 77 of 98 cases (78.6% accuracy); 21 cases were misdiagnosed.
evidence.quote: The model correctly diagnosed MS in 77 cases, achieving an accuracy rate of 78.6%.

evidence.title: Use of large language models as clinical decision support tools for management pancreatic adenocarcinoma using National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of public LLM responses to NCCN-based pancreatic cancer scenarios versus clinician-derived responses
evidence.effect: 42% (n=44) of 104 responses completely correct; ChatGPT 52% correct, 14% inaccurate/misleading; Copilot 33% correct, 25% inaccurate/misleading.
evidence.quote: From the 104 responses, large language model responses were graded as completely correct in 42% of responses (n = 44).

evidence.title: Large language model-generated clinical practice guideline for appendicitis
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on guideline development tasks versus SAGES guideline (AGREE-S)
evidence.effect: LLMs could not independently perform systematic literature search or reliably perform screening, data extraction, or risk of bias assessment. AGREE-S total 119 for LLM-derived guideline vs 156 for SAGES.
evidence.quote: These LLMs were unable to independently perform a systematic literature search or reliably perform screening, data extraction, or risk of bias assessment at the time of testing.
evidence.sample_unit: guidelines (LLM-derived guideline appraised with AGREE-S vs SAGES guideline)

evidence.title: GPT-4 as a Board-Certified Surgeon: A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 exam-style MCQ score versus performance on oral board clinical scenarios
evidence.effect: MCQs: 197/250 (78.8%) correct, 92% probability of passing ABS QE; oral boards: critical failures in 3 of 4 (75%) cases, mainly incorrect timing of intervention and incorrect operation.
evidence.quote: While GPT-4's high performance on MCQs mirrored prior studies, the model struggled to generate accurate long-form content in our mock oral board examination.

evidence.title: Evaluating Locally Run Large Language Models for Obstructive Sleep Apnea Diagnosis and Treatment: A Real-World Polysomnography Study
evidence.outcome: LLM concordance with sleep physician on OSA severity from real-world PSG data
evidence.effect: Gemma2 33% (10/30), Mistral Nemo 47% (14/30), Llama3 50% (15/30) concordance on OSA severity; performance needs significant improvement before real-world implementation.
evidence.quote: Gemma2 showed the lowest concordance of 33% (10/30 patients) with the board-certified sleep physician regarding OSA severity, followed by Mistral Nemo at 47% (14/30 patients) and Llama3 at 50% (15/30 patients).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence in coronary angiography: benchmarking the diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-4o against interventional cardiologists
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o accuracy in identifying lesions requiring intervention and target vessel from static angiogram images
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 71.6%, specificity 57.2% (F1 0.652); target vessel identification 47% from imaging alone, 87% with clinical information.
evidence.quote: However, its accuracy based on static images alone remains below the threshold required for reliable diagnostic and therapeutic support.

evidence.title: Evaluating GPT-4's role in critical patient management in emergency departments
evidence.outcome: Critical error rate of GPT-4 ECG interpretation and patient management in emergency scenarios
evidence.effect: Critical errors in 46% of ECG interpretations (OSCE) and 50% (PubMed); management critical errors 32% (OSCE) and 14% (PubMed); approached 50% when ECG evaluations were included.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 made critical errors in 46% of ECG interpretations in the OSCE group and 50% in the PubMed group.

evidence.title: Advances in Periodontal Diagnostics: Application of MultiModal Language Models in Visual Interpretation of Panoramic Radiographs
evidence.outcome: Agreement of general-purpose multimodal LLMs with clinicians on tooth counts and remaining bone height in panoramic radiographs
evidence.effect: Tooth count agreement was moderate to substantial (kappa 0.52-0.69). RBH was consistently overestimated (best ChatGPT 4.5: +12 pp distal, +11 pp mesial; LoA width ~54-60 pp). Accuracy was insufficient for clinical use.
evidence.quote: In the current stage of development, the ChatGPT models substantially overestimated the RBH values; therefore, they are not applicable for classifying periodontal disease.
evidence.sample_unit: panoramic radiographs (252, 251, 246 and 271 approximal sites for RBH measurement across models)

evidence.title: Assessing DeepSeek-R1 for Clinical Decision Support in Multidisciplinary Laboratory Medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy and completeness on textbook laboratory medicine cases, by question type
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 72.9% (95% CI 69.9-75.7%) and completeness 73.4%; differential diagnosis accuracy only 55.0% versus 85.7% for diagnostic hypotheses.
evidence.quote: Performance varied by question type: the highest accuracy was observed for diagnostic hypotheses (85.7%, 95% CI [81.2%, 89.2%]) and the lowest for differential diagnoses (55.0%, 95% CI [49.3%, 60.5%]).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical cases (each queried 3 times with 3 questions)

evidence.title: A comparative evaluation of publicly available large language models in the assessment of CTG traces according to the FIGO criteria
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy classifying CTG traces as normal or abnormal against clinician FIGO classification
evidence.effect: Gemini 6.7% on normal CTGs; ChatGPT-4.0 46.7% normal and 50% abnormal; Bing Copilot 96.6% normal but 0% abnormal; DeepSeek unable to interpret CTGs.
evidence.quote: Bing Copilot accurately interpreted normal CTGs (96.6%) but failed on abnormal ones (0%).

evidence.title: Evaluating Medium Scale, Open-Source Large Language Models: Towards Decision Support in a Precision Oncology Care Delivery Context
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Gap between benchmark-selected LLM performance and expert-rated real-world oncology performance
evidence.effect: Models chosen on established benchmarks showed modest overall performance on MTB-preparation questions; authors describe a gap between benchmark and real-world performance.
evidence.quote: Common issues include outdated information and confident presentation of misinformation, which indicates a gap between benchmark- and real-world performance.

evidence.title: Large Language Models' Clinical Decision-Making on When to Perform a Kidney Biopsy: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: LLM alignment with nephrologist consensus on kidney biopsy decision questions
evidence.effect: Best models (ChatGPT-3.5, GPT-4) agreed with human mode on only 6 of 11 questions; Llama 2 and MS Copilot on 2 of 11. Propensity scores ranged from 11 (MedLM) to 34 (Claude 3).
evidence.quote: In terms of agreement with the human mode, ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (OpenAI) had the highest levels of alignment, agreeing with the human mode on 6 out of 11 questions.

evidence.title: Large Language Models in Neurological Practice: Real-World Study
evidence.outcome: LLM clinical reasoning and test appropriateness on real-world neurology cases
evidence.effect: Both LLMs showed limitations in nuanced clinical reasoning and overprescribed diagnostic tests in 17%-25% of cases; accuracy 54% (ChatGPT) and 46% (Gemini).
evidence.quote: Both LLMs demonstrated limitations in nuanced clinical reasoning and overprescribed diagnostic tests in 17%-25% of cases.

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models for detecting age-related macular degeneration from retinal imaging
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of general-purpose MLLMs on AMD detection and grading from fundus images
evidence.effect: Binary classification accuracy ranged from 0.301 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to 0.824 (ChatGPT-4o); severity grading accuracy at best 0.463 (Perplexity Sonar Large). Reliability judged insufficient for clinical application.
evidence.quote: In summary, while MLLMs show promise for automated AMD detection and grading from fundus images, their current reliability is insufficient for clinical application, highlighting the need for further model development and validation.
evidence.sample_unit: eyes (ultrawide field fundus images from 76 patients)

evidence.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Diagnose Diabetic Retinopathy from Fundus Photos? A Quantitative Evaluation
evidence.outcome: MLLM diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for diabetic retinopathy detection and grading on fundus images
evidence.effect: Binary DR detection sensitivity: ChatGPT 0.539, Perplexity 0.488, Claude 0.179, Gemini 0.042. Severity grading accuracy 0.314-0.411, sensitivity 0.184-0.247. Performance short of clinical standards.
evidence.quote: Currently, however, there is variability in the accuracy of image analysis, and diagnostic performance falls short of clinical standards for safe implementation in DR diagnosis and grading.

evidence.title: From digital assistants to clinical partners: revolutionizing pediatric urology through large language model-powered decision support and patient education
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on routine versus complex pediatric urology cases
evidence.effect: Accuracy 76% in routine vs 41% in complex cases; GPT-4o3 scored 61.4 vs 51.8 for other models in complex cases.
evidence.quote: LLMs demonstrated superior performance in routine clinical scenarios compared to complex cases (76% vs. 41% accuracy, respectively).

evidence.title: Diagnostic capabilities of large language models in the detection of scaphoid fractures in the emergency department
evidence.venue: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of general-purpose LLMs on scaphoid fracture detection from radiographs
evidence.effect: Claude 3.5 sensitivity 57.1%, Gemini 2.0 18.2%, ChatGPT-4o 9.1%; specificity 43.1%-43.8% across models.
evidence.quote: Claude 3.5 demonstrated superior sensitivity (57.1%) compared to Gemini 2.0 (18.2%) and ChatGPT-4o (9.1%) for fracture detection (p<0.001).

evidence.title: Accuracy of AI-Powered Large Language Models in the Analysis of Laryngeal Images
evidence.venue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
evidence.outcome: Correct primary and differential diagnosis rates of LLMs on laryngeal cases
evidence.effect: Correct primary diagnoses ranged 15.4% to 28.2% and differential diagnoses 15.4% to 25.6%; LLM performance was low.
evidence.quote: The performances of LLMs were low, with correct primary differential diagnoses ranging from 15.4% to 28.2%, and 15.4% to 25.6%, respectively.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Counseling Quality of GPT-4o for Strabismus and Pseudostrabismus in Patient-Generated Mobile Photographs: A Preliminary Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4o for strabismus from patient-generated photos
evidence.effect: Intention-to-diagnose accuracy 14.3% (prompt 1) and 48.6% (prompt 2); per-diagnosis accuracy 33.3% and 63.0%. GPT-4o frequently labeled pseudoesotropia as true strabismus and true strabismus as orthophoria.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o shows poor accuracy for image-based strabismus diagnosis.

evidence.title: Large language model as a clinical decision support tool in the initial management of critically ill children: a pilot evaluation
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on real-world clinical cases across diagnosis, triage, and therapy tasks
evidence.effect: Correct diagnosis in 100% of ED discharge and 95% of PICU 24-h differentials; triage accurate in all PICU cases; therapeutic recommendations appropriate in only 82%.
evidence.quote: Triage decisions were accurate in all PICU cases.

evidence.title: Cautionary lessons from real-world testing of GPT-4.1 AI for pediatric foreign body aspiration
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: General-purpose multimodal model performance on real-world clinical and radiographic data for foreign body aspiration
evidence.effect: Accuracy 62.3%, precision 23.3%, recall 19.0%, F1-score 0.21 on real-world cases against bronchoscopy reference standard.
evidence.quote: The model achieved an overall accuracy of 62.3%, with precision of 23.3%, recall of 19.0%, and an F1-score of 0.21.

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4, Gemini, Claude, and Copilot in Generating Nursing Diagnoses Based on NANDA-I Taxonomy II: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy generating NANDA-I nursing diagnoses from patient scenarios, rated by five experts
evidence.effect: All models performed similarly across domains, with Claude highest overall; small variations and occasional omissions found; authors conclude LLMs are not yet sufficiently reliable for independent clinical use.
evidence.quote: Small variations between models and occasional omissions suggest that expert review is still required before clinical use.

evidence.title: Clinical Accuracy and Safety Concerns Following GPT-5 Public Demonstration in Cancer Care
evidence.outcome: GPT-5 concordance with tumor-board recommendations versus GPT-4o in GI oncology cases
evidence.effect: GPT-5 achieved 85% concordance with tumor-board validation, identical to GPT-4o, contradicting claims of superiority.
evidence.quote: We evaluated GPT-5 against 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases with tumor-board validation and found identical 85% concordance to GPT-4o, contradicting superiority claims.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models Against Multidisciplinary Tumor Boards in Urological Oncology: Results from the Blinded, Prospective CONCORDIA Study
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on intended-use oncology decision support with real-world-like case scenarios
evidence.effect: Neither LLM matched tumor board standards; Claude 0.731 and ChatGPT-4 0.660 versus MTB 0.849; better performance in locally advanced than metastatic cases (p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: Neither LLM matched the MTB standards.

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini in detecting external apical root resorption on panoramic radiographs of orthodontic patients : Artificial intelligence performance in detecting root resorption
evidence.venue: Journal of orofacial orthopedics = Fortschritte der Kieferorthopadie : Organ/official journal Deutsche Gesellschaft fur Kieferorthopadie
evidence.outcome: Agreement and accuracy of general-purpose LLMs versus expert for root resorption severity on radiographs
evidence.effect: GPT-4o kappa 0.371 (binary), accuracy 36.5%, MAE 1.269; Gemini kappa -0.152, accuracy 13.5%, MAE 1.750; both poor for moderate to severe EARR.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, both models showed limited accuracy and agreement, particularly in detecting moderate to severe resorption, and neither can be considered suitable for clinical application at this stage.
evidence.sample_unit: cropped tooth images from panoramic radiographs

evidence.title: Staging Femoral Head Osteonecrosis with General-Purpose AI: Lessons from the Ficat-Arlet Classification
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: General-purpose multimodal model sensitivity, specificity, AUC for Ficat-Arlet staging of femoral head AVN on radiographs
evidence.effect: Micro-averaged sensitivity 25.8%, specificity 79.5%, mean AUC 0.55 across all FA stages; highest sensitivity Stage 0 (54.2%), lowest Stage 4 (10.4%).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o achieved a micro-averaged sensitivity of 25.8%, specificity of 79.5%, and mean AUC of 0.55 across all FA stages.

evidence.title: Performance of large language model in cross-specialty medical scenarios
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic and therapeutic accuracy on clinical vignettes across 12 specialties
evidence.effect: Therapeutic recommendations were inconsistent: GPT-4o median 10 (IQR 0–10), GPT-3.5-Turbo median 0 (IQR 0–6.3; P=.0005), Claude-3-Sonnet median 5 (IQR 0–10); GPT-4o vs Claude P=.45.
evidence.quote: However, their inconsistent performance in generating therapeutic recommendations presents a major barrier to clinical adoption.

evidence.title: Patient safety and quality implications of large language model use in healthcare: a risk-stratified assessment of artificial intelligence-assisted medical consultations
evidence.venue: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
evidence.outcome: LLM response quality across clinical complexity categories using specialist-rated quality indicators
evidence.effect: Routine care scenarios scored 89.2% (95% CI 86.1%-92.3%) versus acute care 65.4% (95% CI 61.8%-69.0%); significant between-group differences (F[3196] = 47.3, P < .001).
evidence.quote: Routine care scenarios achieved excellent performance (89.2%, 95% CI: 86.1%-92.3%), while acute care situations showed concerning limitations (65.4%, 95% CI: 61.8%-69.0%).

evidence.title: AI for evidence-based treatment recommendation in oncology: a blinded evaluation of large language models and agentic workflows
evidence.outcome: Clinical use readiness of LLM recommendations on oncology scenarios
evidence.effect: Clinical use readiness low for all systems: HopeAI 25.3%, o1-preview 6.0%, Claude 2.7%, Gemini 4.0%, Myelo 4.0%.
evidence.quote: Clinical use readiness scores were relatively low for all systems: HopeAI (25.3%), OpenAI o1-preview (6.0%), Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2.7%), Gemini 1.5 Pro (4.0%), and Myelo (4.0%).

evidence.title: Benchmarking GPT-5 in radiation oncology: measurable gains, but persistent need for expert oversight
evidence.outcome: GPT-5 accuracy on exam benchmark versus real-world vignette correctness ratings
evidence.effect: TXIT accuracy 92.8% (GPT-4 78.8%, GPT-3.5 62.1%); vignette correctness mean 3.24/4, with errors clustering in complex scenarios requiring precise trial knowledge or clinical adaptation.
evidence.quote: Errors clustered in complex scenarios requiring precise trial knowledge or detailed clinical adaptation.
evidence.sample_unit: radiation oncology vignettes (plus 300 TXIT multiple-choice items)

evidence.title: Are Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer Answers to Patient Questions Regarding Fecal Incontinence Accurate, Complete, and Consistent With the American Society of Colorectal Surgeons Clinical Practice Guidelines?
evidence.venue: Diseases of the colon and rectum
evidence.outcome: Clinical answer quality of general-purpose chatbot versions against society guidelines
evidence.effect: General-purpose ChatGPT versions failed to give fully accurate/complete/guideline-consistent answers; accuracy ranged 50% to 83%, with GPT-5 Free lowest on accuracy at 50%.
evidence.quote: Reviewers rated 61% of answers accurate, 65% complete, and 68% consistent for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-3.5; 72%, 73%, and 69% for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-4; 50%, 73%, 68% for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 Free; and 83%, 95%, and 82% for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 Plus, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (each presented twice to four ChatGPT versions)

evidence.title: From ChatGPT-4 to ChatGPT-5: Evolving Applications in Pediatric Neoplastic Pathology and Education
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic concordance of deployed LLM configurations on pediatric tumor cases
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o at least partial concordance 27/35 (77.1%), IHC accuracy 74.4%; GPT-5 19/33 (57.6%), IHC accuracy 60.7%; p<0.05 between models.
evidence.quote: GPT-5 showed 19/33 (57.6%) concordance (total and mean 25, 0.76), highest in SRBCT (87.5%) and IHC accuracy 60.7%.

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of large language models for hepatocellular carcinoma treatment recommendations: A nationwide retrospective registry study
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM treatment recommendations with real-world physician decisions in HCC registry
evidence.effect: Concordance rates were 31.1% (ChatGPT 4o), 32.7% (Gemini 2.0), and 26.8% (Claude 3.5); concordance in BCLC-C associated with worse survival (ChatGPT 4o HR 1.650).
evidence.quote: Concordance rates between LLM recommendations and physician decisions were 31.1% (ChatGPT 4o), 32.7% (Gemini 2.0), and 26.8% (Claude 3.5).

evidence.title: Visual Large Language Models in Radiology: A Systematic Multimodel Evaluation of Diagnostic Accuracy and Hallucinations
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and hallucination rates of general-purpose VLLMs on radiology images against reference diagnoses
evidence.effect: Accuracy ranged 8.1% to 29.2% across models; hallucinations 74.4% overall (51.7-82.8% across models); models described as diagnostically unreliable.
evidence.quote: Current VLLMs remain diagnostically unreliable, heavily context-biased, and prone to generating false findings, which limits their clinical suitability.

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT for 12-lead ECG-based localisation of ventricular ectopic foci prior to catheter ablation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4o localising ventricular ectopic foci versus electroanatomical mapping
evidence.effect: ChatGPT correctly localised 17/50 cases (34%), Cohen's κ -0.02 (95% CI -0.18 to 0.14); no fascicular or epicardial origins correctly predicted.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT correctly localised 17/50 cases (34%), yielding an overall Cohen's κ of -0.02 (95% CI -0.18 to 0.14).

evidence.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Cystoscopic Image Interpretation and Bladder Lesion Classification: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: MM-LLM accuracy on clinician-defined cystoscopy stress-test tasks, including difficult differential diagnosis
evidence.effect: OpenAI-o3 satisfaction fell from 84.5% for anatomy to 52.5% for lesion reasoning and 48.2% for final diagnosis; 7-class malignancy accuracy was 62.8%, with performance in difficult differentials modest.
evidence.quote: OpenAI-o3 demonstrated strong reasoning, with high satisfaction for anatomy (339/401, 84.5%) and findings (305/401, 76%), but lower satisfaction for lesion reasoning (211/401, 52.5%) and final diagnosis (193/401, 48.2%), indicating increasing difficulty with higher-order synthesis.
evidence.sample_unit: cystoscopic images (free-text interpretation task; 113 images in classification task)

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT compete with emergency medicine specialists? A two-stage assessment of ECG interpretation supported by clinical information
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of customized GPT on real ED ECGs versus emergency specialists
evidence.effect: ECG Reader-GPT achieved 24% accuracy (27% with clinical information) versus 77% (79%) for emergency medicine specialists.
evidence.quote: In Stage 1, specialists correctly interpreted 77% of ECGs, whereas ECG Reader-GPT achieved 24%.

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of Chinese large language model performance on atrial fibrillation questions
evidence.outcome: Safety, correctness and completeness of Chinese LLM answers to AF patient questions
evidence.effect: Median SCECCE score 10 (IQR 7–10), mean 8.6 (SD 2.0); no significant difference among 7 LLMs (p=0.08). Ernie bot accuracy 87.9%; Doubao safe for 97% of questions.
evidence.quote: Overall, the median SCECCE score was 10[IQR, 7–10] with a mean(SD) score of 8.6(2.0).

evidence.title: Bot vs. doc-who is better at reading proximal humerus fracture x-rays?
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-5 diagnostic accuracy for proximal humerus fracture on shoulder x-rays versus attending reference
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 61.8%, specificity 74.3%, overall accuracy 67.1%; 25.7% of normal x-rays misdiagnosed with fracture or dislocation; 23.5% of isolated PHFx read as normal.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-5 demonstrated a sensitivity of 61.8%, specificity of 74.3%, and an overall accuracy of 67.1% for PHFx x-rays.
evidence.sample_unit: shoulder x-rays (35 proximal humerus fracture, 35 normal)

evidence.title: Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study
evidence.outcome: Whether benchmark and licensing-exam performance predicts real-world performance with human users
evidence.effect: Standard medical knowledge benchmarks and simulated patient interactions did not predict the failures seen with human participants.
evidence.quote: Standard benchmarks for medical knowledge and simulated patient interactions do not predict the failures we find with human participants.

evidence.title: Evaluating the reliability and guideline concordance of ChatGPT-5 in the management of vascular diseases: a cross-sectional expert-based assessment
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated guideline concordance of ChatGPT-5 answers to vascular disease questions
evidence.effect: Mean score 4.74±0.27 on a five-point Likert scale; 40 of 70 questions (57%) received perfect agreement; inter-rater kappa 0.50 (95% CI 0.37-0.64).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-5 achieved a mean score of 4.74±0.27, showing strong consistency with evidence-based recommendations.

evidence.title: Assessing the performance of generative AI chatbots in preimplantation genetic testing: a comparative study of expert evaluations
evidence.outcome: Specialist-rated quality of chatbot answers to PGT questions, by model and question type
evidence.effect: ChatGPT simple 16.83±1.80/25, controversial 27.75±4.49/40; Gemini 14.92±2.02, 26.08±3.99; Llama 13.58±3.60, 16.92±4.96. ChatGPT and Gemini outperformed Llama; performance lower for controversial questions.
evidence.quote: Generative AI shows moderate reliability in addressing PGT-related enquiries, with ChatGPT and Gemini outperforming Llama.
evidence.sample_unit: expert evaluations per chatbot (12 specialists x 13 questions)

evidence.title: Large language models with image processing in automated Cobb angle
evidence.venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of general-purpose multimodal LLMs in Cobb angle measurement versus radiologist reference standard
evidence.effect: Gemini produced no Cobb angles; ChatGPT failed on 90 radiographs (MAE 58.6°±45.9°); Perplexity and Grok mean differences 18.8° and 24.2°; all exceeded the clinically accepted ≤10% difference.
evidence.quote: All AI models demonstrated a difference greater than the clinically accepted difference (≤ 10%).

evidence.title: Can AI safely choose antibiotics over the knife? A STROBE-guided benchmark of GPT-4, GPT-5, and Gemini for non-operative acute appendicitis management
evidence.outcome: Management accuracy of LLMs on intended-use vignettes for non-operative appendicitis candidacy
evidence.effect: Overall MAS differed across models: GPT-5 92% (46/50), GPT-4 84% (42/50), Gemini 76% (38/50); Gemini over-recommended antibiotic trials in appendicolith-positive or abscess-suggestive scenarios.
evidence.quote: Overall MAS differed across models (χ2 = 6.34, p = 0.042): GPT-5 92% (46/50), GPT-4 84% (42/50), and Gemini 76% (38/50).

evidence.title: Accuracy and Knowledge Base Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3 in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: an Expert-Rated Blinded Study
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on guideline-based specialty questions, showing need for domain validation
evidence.effect: Models differed significantly in guideline concordance; ChatGPT and Gemini rarely fully concordant, indicating general-purpose performance may not reflect specialty competence.
evidence.quote: These results highlight the need for ongoing, domain-focused validation before clinical use.

evidence.title: Accuracy of large language models in interpreting urological clinical guidelines: a comparative study with expert evaluation
evidence.outcome: Expert Likert ratings of LLM answers to guideline questions across urological cancers
evidence.effect: Claude 45.9% optimal and 87% optimal/acceptable; Gemini and ChatGPT 68%-70% optimal/acceptable; rephrased prompts did not consistently outperform simple prompts.
evidence.quote: Gemini and ChatGPT showed lower optimal rates but acceptable performance (68%-70% optimal/acceptable).

evidence.title: Evaluation of the applicability of AI chatbots in addressing health management issues for living kidney donors
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and integrity of chatbot answers to living kidney donor FAQs
evidence.effect: Copilot lowest: accuracy 3.35 (3.18, 3.52), integrity 3.40 (3.09, 3.71); ChatGPT-4.0 highest: accuracy 4.05 (3.89, 4.21), integrity 4.00 (3.82, 4.18).
evidence.quote: In contrast, ChatGPT-4.0 achieved the highest median accuracy [4.05 (3.89, 4.21)] and integrity [4.00 (3.82, 4.18)], closely followed by ChatGPT-3.5[4.01 (3.88, 4.16)], [3.98 (3.85, 4.11)].

evidence.title: Publicly available multimodal large language models for ocular surface infections: benchmarking against corneal specialists in triage, diagnosis and treatment
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy on real clinical cases by input modality versus corneal specialists
evidence.effect: Image-only accuracy was lowest (best GPT-5, 61.4%; κ=0.38); text-only GPT-5 83.3% vs specialists 87-90%; treatment accuracy 81-85% vs 90-98%.
evidence.quote: Treatment accuracy remained lower (81-85% vs 90-98%), while urgency triage matched experts in multimodal input.
evidence.sample_unit: microbiologically confirmed infectious keratitis and conjunctivitis cases

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical decision-making performance of large language models in clinically oriented thoracic anatomy scenarios: a comparative evaluation study
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on clinically oriented thoracic anatomy questions rated by expert anatomists (10-point scale)
evidence.effect: Significant differences among models (p < 0.05); Grok median 7.75 vs ChatGPT-4o 4.0, DeepSeek-V2 4.5, Gemini 3.0, so most models scored low on anatomy-based clinical reasoning.
evidence.quote: Post-hoc analysis demonstrated that Grok achieved the highest median score (7.75), significantly outperforming ChatGPT-4o (4.0), DeepSeek-V2 (4.5), and Gemini (3.0), which showed comparable performance.
evidence.sample_unit: open-ended thoracic anatomy questions (each answered by 4 models)

evidence.title: Large Language Model Performance and Clinical Reasoning Tasks
evidence.outcome: Whether multidimensional clinical reasoning benchmark reveals gaps hidden by traditional benchmarks/raw accuracy
evidence.effect: PrIME-LLM provided greater separation than raw accuracy, revealing reasoning gaps obscured by traditional benchmarks; scores ranged 0.64 to 0.78 across 21 LLMs.
evidence.quote: The PrIME-LLM framework provided greater separation than raw accuracy, revealing critical reasoning gaps obscured by traditional benchmarks.

evidence.title: Expert Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Central Auditory Processing Disorder Information
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of chatbot CAPD answers by question difficulty
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy below 4.0 and completeness about 3.5; complex questions often scored below 3.0; only 3 of 44 questions consistently rated >=4 across all three chatbots.
evidence.quote: Current AI chatbots provided generally accurate CAPD information but fell short of clinical standards, particularly on specialized questions.

evidence.title: Comparison of Drug Information Questions' Responses Between Drug Information Pharmacists and Artificial Intelligence Technologies: A Real-World Analysis in a Tertiary Care Hospital
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
evidence.outcome: Composite accuracy and safety scores of AI tools versus pharmacists on real-world drug information questions
evidence.effect: GPT-4o 18.3 and Medical Chat 17.5 comparable to pharmacists 17.7; Gemini 16.7 and Copilot 16.4 lower; Welch ANOVA p<0.001.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o and Medical Chat achieved composite scores comparable to DIC pharmacists (mean [standard deviation (SD)]: 18.3 [2.5], 17.5 [3.1], and 17.7 [3.5], respectively), while Gemini and Copilot showed lower performance (16.7 [3.5] and 16.4 [2.9]).

evidence.title: Performance of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Image-Based Electrocardiogram Interpretation: Exploratory Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Generalist VE-LLM diagnostic accuracy on real-world ECG images versus expert consensus
evidence.effect: Overall balanced accuracy 50.1% to 61.8% across generalist models; AF sensitivity ≤11.1%; QTc sensitivity 0%-45.5%; ST deviation sensitivity <25%; Cohen κ ≤0.39.
evidence.quote: VE-LLMs showed moderate overall performance but mostly low sensitivity and limited agreement with expert ECG interpretation.

evidence.title: AI Chatbot Answers for Drug Dosing Adjustments According to Renal Function in Geriatric Patients Using the New Scoring System (AI Quality Output Score): Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Adequacy of chatbot quality for deployment in high-risk renal dosing
evidence.effect: Even the highest AQUOS achieved is insufficient for deploying AI chatbots in the high-risk health care sector; possible harm rose with lower kidney function and higher medication complexity.
evidence.quote: Even the highest AQUOS achieved is insufficient for deploying AI chatbots in the high-risk health care sector.

evidence.title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Gap between exam-style MCQ accuracy and clinical scenario response quality/safety
